core.name: Executive Sponsor
core.duties: Owns governance at the leadership level, funds it, breaks ties, and removes organizational blockers.

core.name: Business Owner (Committee Lead)
core.duties: Chairs the committee, owns the plan and the policy backlog, approves policies, and reports status to the sponsor.

core.name: {app} Administrator
core.duties: Operates {app}: users, roles, configuration, upgrades and day-to-day enforcement of policies and standards.

core.name: Network & Infrastructure Lead
core.duties: Owns hosting, network, identity integration and platform availability (or the vendor relationship for SaaS).

core.name: Development Lead
core.duties: Owns customizations, integrations, code quality, release practices and technical standards.

core.name: Content / Data Manager
core.duties: Owns the information inside {app}: ownership, quality, lifecycle and author/user standards.

core.name: Business Stakeholder (e.g. Marketing, Operations)
core.duties: Represents the business teams that depend on {app}; brings requirements and validates that standards are workable.

core.name: Internal Communications Lead
core.duties: Owns the communication plan: audiences, messages, channels, timing and feedback loops.

robust.name: Information Security Lead
robust.duties: Owns security policies, risk assessments, vulnerability management and incident response alignment.

robust.name: DevOps / Platform Engineering Lead
robust.duties: Owns CI/CD, environments, infrastructure as code, secrets and deployment controls.

robust.name: Risk & Compliance Officer
robust.duties: Maps policies to regulatory and contractual obligations, owns audits, evidence and exceptions register.

robust.name: Vendor / Procurement Manager
robust.duties: Owns vendor contracts, SLAs, renewals, licensing and third-party risk reviews.

robust.name: Data Protection / Privacy Lead
robust.duties: Owns data classification, privacy impact assessments, retention and data subject requests.

policies.name: Secure Access & Authentication
policies.purpose: Ensure only verified people and systems can reach {app}, using strong, centrally managed authentication.
statements: All users MUST authenticate to {app} through the organization's approved identity provider (single sign-on) where {app} supports it.
Multi-factor authentication MUST be enforced for every account with administrative or elevated privileges, and SHOULD be enforced for all users.
Shared, generic or default accounts MUST NOT be used for interactive access.
Administrative interfaces of {app} MUST NOT be exposed to the public internet without compensating controls.

standards.text: Integrate {app} with the corporate identity provider (SAML/OIDC); disable local accounts except documented break-glass accounts.
Break-glass accounts: maximum two, vaulted credentials, MFA, usage alerted and reviewed within one business day.
Rename or disable vendor default administrator accounts during installation; rotate any default credentials immediately.
Restrict administrative URLs to the corporate network, VPN or zero-trust access proxy; block them at the edge/WAF for public traffic.
Enable the vendor's SSO, MFA enforcement and IP allow-listing options in the {vendor} admin console; document the settings chosen.
Session timeout of 30 minutes idle or less for administrative sessions; all access over TLS 1.2+.

policies.name: Roles, Permissions & Access Reviews
policies.purpose: Grant the least privilege needed for each job and keep it that way over time.
statements: Access to {app} MUST be granted through roles or groups, not assigned directly to individual accounts.
Users MUST receive the minimum permissions required for their role (least privilege).
Privileged roles MUST be limited to named individuals approved by the Business Owner.
Access MUST be reviewed at least quarterly for privileged roles and semi-annually for all roles.
Access MUST be removed within one business day of a role change or departure.

standards.text: Maintain a role catalog for {app}: role name, purpose, permissions summary, approver, and typical members.
Request and approve access through the service desk/ticketing system; the approver is the role owner, never the requester.
Automate provisioning and deprovisioning from the HR/identity system (SCIM or directory group sync) where supported.
Quarterly review: export users and roles, role owners attest, revocations ticketed and evidenced.
Separate duties: users who author or change data SHOULD NOT also approve their own changes in workflows.

policies.name: Content & Data Ownership and Lifecycle
policies.purpose: Make sure every piece of information in {app} has an owner, stays accurate, and is retired on time.
statements: Every major content area, data set or module in {app} MUST have a named business owner.
Owners MUST review their content/data for accuracy at a defined interval.
Information MUST be retained and disposed of according to the organization's retention schedule.
Obsolete content/data MUST be archived or removed rather than left active.

standards.text: Maintain an ownership register: area, owner, backup owner, review interval, retention rule.
Default review interval: 12 months for general content, 6 months for regulated or customer-facing information.
Use {app}'s workflow, expiry or archival features where available; otherwise run a scheduled stale-content report.
Naming and structure conventions documented in a style guide and enforced at creation (templates, required fields, validation).

metrics: % of areas with a named owner

policies.name: Change & Release Management
policies.purpose: Change {app} predictably so that releases don't surprise users or break production.
statements: All changes to {app} configuration, code, integrations or structure in production MUST follow the approved change process.
Changes MUST be tested in a non-production environment before production unless classified as an emergency change.
Emergency changes MUST be documented and retroactively reviewed within five business days.
Every production change MUST have a rollback plan.

standards.text: Classify changes: standard (pre-approved, low risk), normal (committee or CAB approval), emergency (post-review).
Minimum environments: development/test and production; staging/UAT for customer-facing or high-risk systems.
Release notes published to affected users for any user-visible change; maintenance windows communicated at least 3 business days ahead.
Track vendor release schedules and assess each release for impact before it reaches production.
Freeze periods defined for peak business events.

policies.name: Configuration & Customization Standards
policies.purpose: Keep {app} maintainable and upgradeable by controlling how it is configured and extended.
statements: Customizations and extensions to {app} MUST be approved by the Development Lead before build.
Out-of-the-box capabilities SHOULD be preferred over custom development.
All custom code, configuration-as-code and scripts MUST be stored in version control.
Third-party add-ons, plugins or modules MUST be approved before installation.

standards.text: Document a design decision record for every significant customization: need, options considered, upgrade impact.
Follow {vendor}'s documented extension points and supported APIs; unsupported modifications are prohibited.
Maintain an add-on/plugin register: name, version, owner, purpose, support status, renewal date.
Code review required for all custom code; automated linting/tests in the build where feasible.

policies.name: Patching, Upgrades & Vendor Support Lifecycle
policies.purpose: Keep {app} on supported, patched versions to limit security and support risk.
statements: {app} MUST run on a version supported by the vendor.
Security patches MUST be applied within defined timeframes based on severity.
An upgrade roadmap MUST be maintained showing support end dates and planned upgrades.
The organization MUST subscribe to {vendor} security and release notifications.

standards.text: Patch timeframes: critical 7 days, high 30 days, medium 90 days, low next scheduled release (adjust to your risk appetite).
Track the vendor's lifecycle page; plan upgrades at least 6 months before end of mainstream support.
For SaaS, track the vendor's release calendar, test new releases in a sandbox/preview tenant, and review deprecation notices monthly.
Maintain a lifecycle register: component, version, support phase, end date, next action.

policies.name: Backup & Recovery
policies.purpose: Recover {app} and its data within agreed times after failure, error or attack.
statements: {app} data and configuration MUST be backed up according to a defined schedule.
Recovery time and recovery point objectives (RTO/RPO) MUST be defined and approved by the Business Owner.
Restores MUST be tested at least annually.
Backups MUST be protected from unauthorized access and from ransomware (isolated or immutable copies).

standards.text: Default objectives (adjust per business impact): RPO 24 hours, RTO 8 hours for internal systems; RPO 1 hour, RTO 4 hours for customer-facing systems.
Backups encrypted at rest; at least one copy offsite/another region and one immutable or offline.
Confirm the vendor's backup scope, retention and restore process in the contract; export critical data on a schedule to an organization-controlled store.
Annual restore test documented with achieved RTO/RPO and remediation items.

policies.name: Monitoring, Incident Response & Escalation
policies.purpose: Detect problems with {app} quickly and make sure everyone knows who to call and what happens next.
statements: {app} availability and key functions MUST be monitored.
Incidents MUST be classified by severity and handled according to the escalation matrix.
Severity 1 incidents MUST have a post-incident review within five business days.
Users MUST have a single, published channel to report problems.

standards.text: Severity definitions: Sev 1 = {app} down or data at risk for many users; Sev 2 = major function impaired; Sev 3 = minor/workaround exists; Sev 4 = request/cosmetic.
Escalation matrix published (role, primary, backup, contact method, response target) and tested twice a year.
Synthetic uptime checks and alerting on error rate, response time and failed jobs; alerts route to an on-call rotation for Sev 1/2.
Know the vendor support path: support tiers, contract number, how to open a priority case, and expected response times.
Status updates to users every 60 minutes during Sev 1 through the communication channel defined in this plan.

policies.name: Integrations & API Usage
policies.purpose: Connect {app} to other systems securely, reliably and with clear ownership.
statements: Every integration with {app} MUST be registered with an owner, purpose, data exchanged and authentication method.
Integrations MUST use dedicated service identities with least privilege, never personal accounts.
Credentials and API keys MUST be stored in an approved secrets store, never in code or documents.
Integrations MUST be monitored for failure.

standards.text: Integration register fields: name, systems, direction, data classification, auth method, owner, SLA, monitoring link.
Use the vendor's supported APIs; respect documented rate limits and implement retries with back-off.
Rotate integration credentials at least annually or on personnel change.
New integrations reviewed by the Development Lead (and Security Lead in the robust pack) before production.

policies.name: Training, Onboarding & Offboarding
policies.purpose: Make sure people know how to use {app} correctly and lose access when they no longer need it.
statements: Users MUST complete role-appropriate {app} training before receiving access.
Administrators MUST complete administrator training and read this governance plan.
Offboarding MUST remove access and transfer ownership of content, data and integrations.
Training material MUST be kept current with the deployed version.

standards.text: Maintain role-based quick-start guides and a recorded walkthrough for each role in the role catalog.
Access request form includes training completion confirmation.
Offboarding checklist: disable account, revoke tokens, reassign owned items/workflows, transfer integration ownership.
Annual refresher for administrators, including policy changes from the past year.

policies.name: Information Security & Vulnerability Management
policies.purpose: Identify and remediate security weaknesses across the platform before they are exploited.
statements: Systems in scope MUST be scanned for vulnerabilities on a defined schedule.
Vulnerabilities MUST be remediated within severity-based timeframes or have an approved exception.
Security testing MUST occur before major releases and at least annually for internet-facing systems.
Security risks MUST be recorded in the risk register with an owner.

standards.text: Authenticated vulnerability scans monthly for servers and containers; continuous dependency scanning in CI.
Annual third-party penetration test for internet-facing systems; findings tracked to closure.
Review the vendor's SOC 2 / ISO 27001 report annually and track complementary user entity controls (CUECs).
Remediation SLA aligned with P-06 patch timeframes; exceptions require Security Lead approval and expiry date.

policies.name: Network Architecture & Segmentation
policies.purpose: Limit exposure and blast radius through deliberate network design.
statements: Systems MUST be placed in network zones according to their exposure and data sensitivity.
Traffic between zones MUST be denied by default and allowed only by documented rules.
Network diagrams MUST be maintained and reviewed at least annually.
Firewall and security group rules MUST be reviewed at least semi-annually.

standards.text: Minimum zones: public/edge (CDN, WAF), application, data, and management; administrative interfaces only in the management zone.
Use private endpoints / service endpoints for PaaS data services; disable public network access where supported.
Every firewall/NSG rule has an owner, ticket reference and review date; any-any rules prohibited.
Document data flows between {app} and other systems in the network diagram, including vendor-hosted endpoints.

policies.name: Perimeter, Remote Access & Edge Protection
policies.purpose: Control how users and attackers can reach systems from outside the organization.
statements: Remote administrative access MUST use approved remote access methods (VPN or zero-trust access) with MFA.
Internet-facing applications MUST be protected by a web application firewall or equivalent edge controls.
Direct RDP/SSH exposure to the internet is prohibited.
TLS MUST be enforced for all external traffic with current, approved configurations.

standards.text: WAF in prevention mode with managed rule sets; bot and rate-limit protection on login and search endpoints.
Use bastion/jump hosts or just-in-time access for server administration.
TLS 1.2 minimum (1.3 preferred); HSTS enabled; certificates auto-renewed and monitored for expiry.
Restrict vendor admin consoles by IP or conditional access policies where the vendor supports it.

policies.name: Privileged Access Management
policies.purpose: Tightly control and record the most powerful access across the platform.
statements: Privileged access to infrastructure, databases and administrative consoles MUST be granted just-in-time or through a privileged access management (PAM) tool.
Privileged sessions SHOULD be recorded or logged in detail.
Standing privileged access MUST be minimized and justified.
Privileged credentials MUST be vaulted and rotated.

standards.text: Separate admin accounts from daily-use accounts for all privileged users.
Just-in-time elevation with approval and time limits (e.g. 4 hours) for production administration.
Vaulted shared credentials rotated after each use or at least every 90 days.
Monthly report of privileged role assignments reviewed by the Security Lead.

policies.name: Source Control & CI/CD
policies.purpose: Build and deploy changes through automated, traceable and gated pipelines.
statements: All code, configuration and infrastructure definitions MUST be stored in the approved source control system.
Production deployments MUST be performed by automated pipelines, not by hand.
Pipelines MUST include automated quality and security gates.
Every production deployment MUST be traceable to an approved change and a reviewed commit.

standards.text: Protected main branch: pull requests required, at least one reviewer, passing checks, no force-push.
Pipeline gates: build, unit tests, linting, dependency/vulnerability scan, secret scan; production stage requires manual approval.
Pin tool and dependency versions; store build artifacts immutably with provenance.
Deployment logs retained for at least 12 months as change evidence.

policies.name: Environment Management & Test Data
policies.purpose: Keep environments consistent, purposeful and free of uncontrolled production data.
statements: Each environment MUST have a defined purpose, owner and access policy.
Production data MUST NOT be copied to lower environments unless masked or anonymized, or explicitly approved.
Environments SHOULD be provisioned from code to ensure parity.
Unused environments MUST be decommissioned.

standards.text: Environment register: name, purpose, owner, data classification, access group, cost center.
Data masking procedure documented for any production-to-test refresh; refreshes logged.
Infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform, Bicep, CloudFormation) for all non-SaaS environments.
Quarterly review of environments for cost and continued need.

policies.name: Secrets & Key Management
policies.purpose: Protect credentials, keys and certificates throughout their lifecycle.
statements: Secrets MUST be stored only in approved secret management systems.
Secrets MUST NOT be committed to source control, embedded in images or shared via chat/email.
Encryption keys and certificates MUST have owners, rotation schedules and expiry monitoring.
Exposed secrets MUST be rotated immediately and treated as security incidents.

standards.text: Use a managed vault (e.g. Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault) with access via workload identity.
Automated secret scanning on every commit and pull request; block merges on findings.
Rotation: service credentials at least annually, high-privilege secrets every 90 days, certificates before expiry with 30-day alerts.

policies.name: Logging, Audit Trails & Security Monitoring
policies.purpose: Record who did what, detect suspicious activity, and preserve evidence.
statements: Authentication, administrative actions and data access for {app} MUST be logged.
Logs MUST be centralized, protected from tampering and retained per the retention schedule.
Security-relevant events MUST be monitored and alerted.
Logs MUST NOT contain secrets or unnecessary personal data.

standards.text: Forward {app} audit logs and platform logs to the central log/SIEM platform.
Retention: 90 days hot, 12 months total minimum (longer where regulation requires).
Alert on: privileged role changes, MFA disabled, mass export/deletion, logins from unusual locations, repeated failed logins.
Enable the vendor's audit log/event monitoring features and export them before the vendor's retention window ends.

policies.name: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
policies.purpose: Keep critical business services running, or restore them, during a major disruption.
statements: A business impact analysis MUST classify {app} by criticality.
A disaster recovery plan MUST exist for {app} consistent with its criticality and approved RTO/RPO.
DR plans MUST be tested at least annually.
Manual workarounds for critical processes MUST be documented.

standards.text: Criticality tiers: Tier 1 (RTO ≤ 4h), Tier 2 (≤ 24h), Tier 3 (≤ 72h); DR design matched to tier.
Secondary region/site for Tier 1 systems with documented failover and failback runbooks.
Obtain the vendor's BC/DR summary and test results; document an exit/continuity plan if the vendor fails.
Annual DR exercise (tabletop at minimum; technical failover for Tier 1) with lessons learned.

policies.name: Data Classification, Privacy & Retention
policies.purpose: Handle data according to its sensitivity and legal obligations.
statements: All data in {app} MUST be classified using the organization's classification scheme.
Handling controls (encryption, access, sharing) MUST match the classification.
Personal data processing MUST have a lawful basis and be recorded where required.
Data MUST be deleted or anonymized when its retention period ends.

standards.text: Classification levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted; label at the data set or module level in {app}.
Encryption at rest and in transit for Confidential and Restricted data.
Privacy impact assessment for new processing of personal data in {app}.
Documented process to handle data subject requests (access, correction, deletion) affecting {app}.

metrics: Data subject requests closed on time

policies.name: Third-Party & Vendor Risk Management
policies.purpose: Understand and manage the risk introduced by vendors and their sub-processors.
statements: Vendors providing or supporting {app} MUST undergo a risk assessment before contract and at renewal.
Contracts MUST include security, privacy, SLA and exit provisions appropriate to the risk.
Vendor security attestations MUST be reviewed at least annually.
Vendor access to organizational systems MUST follow P-02 and P-14.

standards.text: Vendor tiering by data access and criticality; questionnaire depth matched to tier.
Contract checklist: data location, breach notification time, sub-processor list, audit rights, data return/deletion on exit, SLA credits.
Track vendor SLAs monthly and review performance at least quarterly.

policies.name: Asset, License & Cost Management
policies.purpose: Know what you run, what you pay for, and whether it is used.
statements: All components, licenses and subscriptions supporting {app} MUST be recorded in the asset inventory.
License usage MUST be reviewed at least semi-annually against entitlements.
Cloud spend for {app} MUST be tagged, budgeted and monitored.
Renewals MUST be reviewed at least 90 days before the renewal date.

standards.text: Asset inventory fields: component, version, owner, environment, license type, cost, renewal date.
Mandatory resource tags: application, environment, owner, cost-center.
Budget alerts at 80% and 100% of monthly forecast; monthly cost review with the Business Owner.
Reclaim inactive user licenses after 60 days of inactivity.

policies.name: Capacity & Performance Management
policies.purpose: Keep {app} fast and available as usage grows.
statements: Performance and capacity targets for {app} MUST be defined.
Capacity MUST be reviewed against forecasts before major business events and at least quarterly.
Significant releases SHOULD include performance testing.
Performance degradations MUST be treated as incidents per P-08.

standards.text: Targets: e.g. 95th percentile page/API response under 2 seconds; availability 99.9% monthly for customer-facing services.
Load test before peak events and major releases; autoscaling limits documented.
Track vendor-imposed limits (API rate limits, storage, users) and alert at 80% consumption.

policies.name: Acceptable Use & AI Usage
policies.purpose: Set clear expectations for how people use {app}, related data, and AI tools.
statements: Users MUST use {app} only for authorized business purposes.
Confidential or Restricted data MUST NOT be entered into AI tools that are not approved for that classification.
AI-generated content published through {app} MUST be reviewed by a human accountable for its accuracy.
AI features within {app} MUST be assessed and approved before enablement.

standards.text: Publish an approved AI tools list with permitted data classifications for each.
Label or disclose AI-generated content where required by law, contract or brand policy.
Review vendor AI feature terms: data retention, model training on customer data, regional processing.

policies.name: Compliance, Audit & Exceptions
policies.purpose: Show, with evidence, that policies are followed, and manage deviations deliberately.
statements: Applicable regulatory and contractual obligations MUST be mapped to policies in this plan.
Evidence of control operation MUST be collected and retained.
Deviations from any policy MUST be handled through the exceptions process with risk acceptance and expiry.
Internal reviews of policy compliance MUST occur at least annually.

standards.text: Maintain a control matrix: obligation → policy → standard → evidence → owner → frequency.
Exceptions register: policy, requester, justification, compensating controls, risk owner, approval, expiry (max 12 months).
Evidence stored in a central, access-controlled repository organized by policy ID and period.

policies.name: Architecture Review & Technical Debt
policies.purpose: Make significant technical decisions deliberately and keep debt visible.
statements: Significant architecture changes to {app} or its surroundings MUST be reviewed before implementation.
Architecture decisions MUST be recorded.
Technical debt MUST be tracked and prioritized alongside feature work.
Reference architectures and approved technology lists SHOULD guide new work.

standards.text: Architecture decision records (ADRs) stored with the code or in a shared repository.
Review triggers: new integration, new data store, change in hosting, new external exposure, new vendor.
Reserve a defined share of delivery capacity (e.g. 15–20%) for technical debt and upgrades.

policies.name: Cloud Governance & Guardrails
policies.purpose: Apply consistent, automated guardrails to cloud resources supporting {app}.
statements: Cloud resources MUST be deployed within approved accounts/subscriptions, regions and services.
Preventive guardrails (policy as code) MUST enforce baseline security settings.
Public exposure of storage, databases and management endpoints MUST be blocked by default.
Cloud configuration MUST be continuously assessed against a security baseline.

standards.text: Landing zone with separate accounts/subscriptions per environment; centralized identity and logging.
Policy as code (e.g. Azure Policy, AWS SCPs/Config, OPA) enforcing encryption, tagging, allowed regions and no public storage.
Cloud security posture management with findings triaged weekly.
For SaaS-only estates, apply this policy to any supporting cloud services (integration platforms, storage, functions).

policies.name: Endpoint & Workstation Security
policies.purpose: Make sure the devices used to access and administer {app} are trustworthy.
statements: Devices used to access {app} MUST meet the organization's device security baseline.
Administrative access SHOULD come only from managed devices.
Lost or stolen devices MUST be reported immediately and remotely wiped where possible.
Removable media use for Restricted data MUST be controlled.

standards.text: Managed device baseline: disk encryption, EDR, OS patching, screen lock, firewall.
Conditional access: require compliant devices for administrative roles and for Restricted data.
Privileged access workstations (or hardened profiles) for infrastructure administrators.
